speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me determine the cause, have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash, such as lines or a "lace-like" appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema infectiosum (Fifth disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The specific combination of a "lace-like" rash on the trunk and extremities, a facial rash sparing the mouth, and a preceding viral prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea is classic for this condition. Given the clinical picture is highly specific, no further questions or tests are required.
